question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` plus `defaultAccount` as a supported public configuration and setup contract?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but adding a permanent channel configuration model and changing setup output requires explicit maintainer product and compatibility ownership.

options.title: Sponsor and reopen
options.body: Adopt the shared named-account model and complete final owner review of upgrade, authentication, policy, and state isolation behavior.

options.title: Keep Teams single-account
options.body: Decline the new public configuration surface and continue requiring separate gateways for separate Teams bot identities.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Sponsor a smaller follow-up after defining which settings may inherit and which identity or state fields must remain account-local.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and reopen
recommendation.body: Adopt the shared named-account model and complete final owner review of upgrade, authentication, policy, and state isolation behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal spans the Teams runtime, configuration, plugin architecture, setup-adjacent policy, and persistent-state surfaces affected by this decision.
